c1-06-01.title: Communicative Challenge: A Double-Edged Technology
c1-06-01.scenario: You are talking with a colleague about a new technology that brings great chances and great risks.
c1-06-01.prompt: Say what kind of thing the technology is, using a fixed metaphor.
cues: Use the metaphor for chance and risk
c1-06-01.target: Ez az új technológia kétélű fegyver: lehetőség is, kockázat is.
c1-06-01.english: This new technology is a double-edged sword: both an opportunity and a risk.
c1-06-01.canDo: I can use fixed metaphors such as *kétélű fegyver*, *sarokkő*, *vízválasztó* and *zsákutca*.

c1-06-02.title: Communicative Challenge: What Makes a Good Leader
c1-06-02.scenario: A colleague asks you what makes a good leader.
c1-06-02.prompt: Name two qualities with abstract nouns.
c1-06-02.target: A jó vezetőnek jó valóságérzékre és nagy felelősségtudatra van szüksége.
c1-06-02.english: A good leader needs a good sense of reality and a great sense of responsibility.
c1-06-02.canDo: I can form abstract nouns with *-érzék*, *-tudat* and *-rend* (*valóságérzék*, *felelősségtudat*, *értékrend*).

c1-06-03.title: Communicative Challenge: Why the Project Failed
c1-06-03.scenario: A friend asks why the project failed. There were too many rules.
c1-06-03.prompt: Say with figurative verbs what the rules did and how the project ended.
cues: Say the rules tied the project
c1-06-03.target: A sok szabály gúzsba kötötte a projektet, ezért az zátonyra futott.
c1-06-03.english: The many rules shackled the project, so it ran aground.
c1-06-03.canDo: I can use figurative verbs such as *hidat ver*, *zátonyra fut* and *gúzsba köt*.

c1-06-04.title: Communicative Challenge: A Lean Style
c1-06-04.scenario: You have read a short text without decoration, and a friend asks what you think of its style.
c1-06-04.prompt: Say that the style is lean and why that works.
c1-06-04.target: A szöveg szikár, de éppen ezért erős: minden szónak súlya van.
c1-06-04.english: The text is lean, but that is exactly why it is strong: every word has weight.
c1-06-04.canDo: I can explain in simple Hungarian what *szikár* prose is.

c1-06-05.title: Communicative Challenge: What the Text Says About Silence
c1-06-05.scenario: You have read a short text about János Pilinszky, and a friend asks what it says about silence.
c1-06-05.prompt: Tell your friend what the text says about silence and words.
cues: Say where the greatest words come from
c1-06-05.target: A szöveg szerint a legnagyobb szavak a csendből születnek meg.
c1-06-05.english: According to the text, the greatest words are born out of silence.
c1-06-05.canDo: I can say what the text about Pilinszky says about silence and a plain style.

c1-06-consolidation.title: Communicative Challenge: A Turning Point
c1-06-consolidation.scenario: A friend asks you about yesterday's debate on a new decision.
c1-06-consolidation.prompt: Say that the decision was a turning point, but the debate ran aground.
cues: Name the decision with a metaphor
Say what happened to the debate
c1-06-consolidation.target: A döntés vízválasztó volt, de a vita végül zátonyra futott.
c1-06-consolidation.english: The decision was a watershed, but the debate eventually ran aground.
c1-06-consolidation.canDo: I can use fixed metaphors such as *kétélű fegyver*, *sarokkő* and *vízválasztó*.
